sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for roughly a third of the model's importance, and risk rises as utilization rises.
The steepest increase comes at high utilization, where the risk contribution jumps sharply once utilization passes about 72% of the credit limit.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency on file raises the predicted risk.
Higher income lowers predicted risk, though its effect is moderate at most.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies, so applicants with both high utilization and delinquencies carry the most risk.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, with longer histories associated with lower risk.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio affects default risk at this sample size.
Number of dependents, age, months at address and recent credit inquiries hardly matter.
